evidence: Only 2 packages ('javalang' and 'javalang.test') suggest a single deployment unit with internal modularity
Clear separation of concerns into cohesive modules: tokenizer, parser, ast, tree, javadoc, util, parse
Hierarchical module dependencies (e.g., parse.py imports from parser and tokenizer, parser imports tokenizer and util)
Tree and AST modules use inheritance hierarchies typical of domain modeling in monoliths
No external communication patterns (e.g., REST, RPC) or service boundaries visible
Directory depth of 3 reflects logical module grouping (javalang/submodule/test)
Low average fan-out (1.4) indicates tight internal cohesion and limited cross-module coupling
risks: Risk of temporal coupling if initialization order between modules (e.g., parser, ast, tree) is not explicit
Potential for module boundary leakage if internal dependencies across submodules (e.g., tree -> ast) become overly complex
Difficulty scaling development across teams due to shared codebase without physical service boundaries
